purpose: Minimal integration boundary: AutoLoop keeps Graph topology, scheduler policy, task decomposition, writer authority, review/repair, evidence, CBM, telemetry, and Controller authority. A third-party durable engine — if ever selected — may ONLY provide lifecycle durability / recovery mechanics behind this contract. The provider is a seam, never the AutoLoop brain.

createExecution.in: { executionId, sourceDigest, configDigest, irDigest, timeoutMs, maxRepairAttempts }
createExecution.semantics: idempotent: same executionId returns the existing execution

persistCheckpoint.in: { executionId, checkpoint: { phaseStates, phaseAttempts, phaseResultHashes, completedPhaseIds, activePhase, activeLifecycleStage, writerPhaseActive, writerLeaseHolder, expectedRevision } }
persistCheckpoint.semantics: atomic; CAS revision; must never partially write

resumeExecution.out: { resumed, state: RUNNING | COMPLETED | RECOVERY_REQUIRED | RESTART_REQUIRED | CORRUPT }
resumeExecution.semantics: never re-decomposes; never re-runs completed phases; writer interruption -> RECOVERY_REQUIRED

markNodeStarted.semantics: journaled before the node's first adapter call

markNodeCompleted.semantics: journaled + checkpointed before successor scheduling; D1/D2 gate

recover.semantics: rebuild ready set from durable truth (D5)

hardRules: provider may never modify Graph topology, scheduler policy, writer authority, memory trust model, or model routing
a provider failure must degrade to HOLD with a structured status — never change the graph outcome

mapping.cleanup: colima runtime container cleanup + worktree revoke (idempotent)

currentMapping.note: STACK_A already implements every provider method natively. The production Graph path (STACK_B) does not use any provider — wiring STACK_A's provider behind runColimaGraph is the bounded-hardening path (DE-2 candidate).

selectionBoundary: Temporal/Restate would implement the SAME contract behind this seam; AutoLoop retains all policy. Integration boundary: AutoLoop Graph -> DurableExecutionProvider -> backend.
